AuthnSessionItem.description: One live session of the caller's, as the listing reports it.

client_ip.description: Empty when the session carries none

created_at.description: When the session was created, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

current.description: Whether this is the session the request came with

expires_at.description: The absolute expiry, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. A browser session can stop being valid earlier, once its idle timeout passes.

id.description: The public session identifier; it names the row and is not a credential.

kind.description: The session kind, browser or token; service-account sessions are never listed.

last_seen_at.description: Last activity of the session, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. For a browser session this is the last use the row was written for: touches are coalesced, written at most once per effective touch interval — the configured interval capped at half the idle timeout — so the value lags the newest use by up to that interval. A token session has no renewal path, so its value is the creation time.

user_agent.description: Empty when the session carries none

AuthnSessionList.description: The caller's own live sessions, in the order the listing reports them.

sessions.description: The live browser and token sessions of the account, most recently created first; the empty array when there are none.

AuthnSessionRevoked.description: The outcome of revoking every session of the caller's but the current one.

AuthnSessionView.description: Whether the request carries a signed-in identity and, when it does, the facts the identity is built from.

account_id.description: The account the request is taken to be from; the impersonated account while impersonating

actor_id.description: The account whose hands are on the request; present only while impersonating

assurance.description: The assurance level the authentication reached; "none" when the identity carries no level.

auth_time.description: The instant of the last interactive authentication, absent when the identity carries none

authenticated.description: False when nobody is signed in; every other field is then absent

impersonating.description: True only while the identity is impersonating another account; absent otherwise.

methods.description: The authentication methods the identity completed, each from the closed set named by the enum; absent when the session records none.

provider.description: The backend that verified the credential

session_id.description: The public identifier of the session the request came with; absent when nobody is signed in.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

post.description: Revokes the session the request's credential belongs to and writes a Set-Cookie header that has the browser drop the session cookie. When the identity is impersonating, the session revoked is the administrator's own, the one the credential belongs to, so the impersonation ends with it. A repeated call from the same credential is answered 401 on the replica that revoked the session, which clears its verification cache as it revokes. Another replica can still accept it while its own check cache holds (check-ttl, five seconds by default), unless the revocation event clears that entry first; such a call is answered 204, and it clears that replica's cache too, so a further call there is 401 as well.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

503.description: The session store could not be reached

post.summary: Revoke the session the request came with and clear its cookie

get.description: Answers whether the request carries a signed-in identity and, when it does, the facts about it. It may be called without a credential: that answer is {"authenticated": false} rather than a 401, so a front end can ask on startup; a credential that is presented and does not hold is still a 401. An impersonating identity is answered here, naming both the impersonated account and the actor.

200.description: The identity on the request, or that nobody is signed in

401.description: A credential was presented and does not hold

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

get.summary: Who is signed in on this session

delete.description: Revokes every unrevoked browser and token session of the caller's account except the one the request came with, in a single statement, and answers with the number of rows it changed. Expiry is not a condition: a session past its expiry that was never revoked is revoked and counted too. Service-account sessions are untouched. An impersonating identity revokes the impersonated account's sessions; the operator's own session is outside that set and stays.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

503.description: The session store could not be reached

delete.summary: Revoke every session of the caller's but the current one

get.description: Lists the caller's own live browser and token sessions, most recently created first (by creation instant, then by identifier), with the current one flagged. Service-account sessions are not listed, and the list is not paginated: every live session of the account is returned. An impersonating identity lists the impersonated account's sessions, never the operator's own.

200.description: The page of the caller's sessions

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

503.description: The session store could not be reached

get.summary: List the caller's own live sessions

delete.description: Revokes one of the caller's own sessions. A session that does not exist, belongs to another account, or is a service-account session is answered with the same 403, so the route does not reveal which identifiers exist. Revoking the current session also writes a Set-Cookie header that has the browser drop the session cookie. Revoking an already revoked session of the caller's succeeds.

parameters.description: The public session identifier, as returned in the session listing. It names the row and is not a credential.
parameters.name: id

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The session is not the caller's, does not exist, or is a service-account session

503.description: The session store could not be reached

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's own sessions
